statements.status_notes: ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio() did not check server_hostname the way wrap_socket() does, so with check_hostname enabled and no server_hostname supplied, hostname verification was silently skipped. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/156793 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/869069d52ce0efab2f8c38197e92cdaaa312f1ed), first released in CPython 3.12.15; see the advisory https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/QNZRG3YOAMTHDCMVCICXGY6YEFPY2VDL/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-19553. On the 3.12 branch upstream made the new check a DeprecationWarning instead of the ValueError raised in 3.13 and later: with check_hostname enabled and no server_hostname, wrap_bio() in 3.12.15 and later warns ('check_hostname requires server_hostname') but still creates the SSL object without a hostname to verify. Applications on 3.12 are protected only if they pass server_hostname to wrap_bio() (or turn that DeprecationWarning into an error); the CVE record nonetheless lists 3.12.15 as the first fixed 3.12 release, which this status follows. The DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.12 package is fixed from 3.12.15-r0, the first published build of CPython 3.12.15 (the version string in libpython3.12.so); no earlier published build carries a backport. Compared Lib/ssl.py in the python-3.12 package in every published build on x86_64 and aarch64 (3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4) with the file in the matching upstream CPython release, and read the differences: 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.14-r2 ship the upstream file for their version, in every case without the server_hostname check that the fix adds to SSLObject._create(); 3.12.15-r0 to 3.12.16-r4 ship the upstream 3.12.15 or later file unchanged, which has it.
